rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.fn` only declares a signature: `Sources::search_text(&self, query: &TextQuery) -> Result<TextMatches, SourceError>` is async and searches available project files. Search behavior and inputs belong to the sibling requirements `search_text.behavior` and `search_text.inputs`, so I did not assess them here.

The signature has three testable parts. Each is exercised by a test marked `{test}` for this requirement:

- **Async method on `Sources` taking `&TextQuery`.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` calls `sources.search_text(&TextQuery::new(...)).await` directly on a `Sources` value. It does this with default scope and with `.scope(SourceScope::under(..))`, so it compiles against the declared signature.
- **`Ok(TextMatches)` on success.** The same test asserts on `found.complete` and on `found.matches` (length, and `path` in the scoped case). This shows the success value is a `TextMatches` with those fields and that the search covers available files. Files excluded by gitignore rules or under `.git` are not returned.
- **`Err(SourceError)` on failure.** The same test asserts `search_text` with scope `under("..")` returns `is_err()`. This covers the error arm of the `Result`.

Two further tests reach the method through the tool layer:

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[fixed_tools_deliver_domain_contents_with_mandatory_snapshot_dependencies]` dispatches `search_text` and asserts the exact match output.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[source_discovery_and_its_pages_do_not_register_reads]` dispatches `search_text` and pages through the results.

Because the requirement is signature-only and the signature has no conditional logic of its own, I found no unmet obligation. I found no test-adequacy or marking gap.

text: pub async fn search_text(&self, query: &TextQuery) -> Result<TextMatches, SourceError>;
